note.question: How should economic losses with targeted closures be reduced?
note.overview: Data on population movements can be helpful in designing targeted policy responses to curb epidemic spread. However, it is not clear how to exactly leverage such data and how valuable they might be for the control of epidemics. To explore these questions, we study a spatial epidemic model that explicitly accounts for population movements and propose an optimization framework for obtaining targeted policies that restrict economic activity in different neighborhoods of a city at different levels.

source.quote: Data on population movements can be helpful in designing targeted policy responses to curb epidemic spread.

The spatial nature of epidemic spread and our model admit a natural network representation in which nodes correspond to different locations/neighborhoods and (weighted) edges encode trips of individuals between these neighborhoods.

Chen et al. (2020) focus on an age-structured SAPHIRE (susceptible, exposed, presymptomatic infectious, ascertained infectious, unascertained infectious, isolated, removed) model and study how to allocate COVID-19 vaccines to different age groups subject to a limited supply constraint.
